reviews.body:
What an unexpected hidden gem! From the outside, Front Street Cafe looks like a cozy, small-town mom-and-pop restaurant, so we really had no idea what to expect when we walked in. We were so pleasantly surprised to find out that they focus on organic, non-GMO, natural ingredients, farm-to-table food, and make everything from scratch.

The food was absolutely amazing! I had the ribeye and it was one of the best I’ve had! It was cooked perfectly and full of flavor. The vegetables were fresh and delicious, the salad was wonderful, as well as the rolls and butter ( might just top Texas Roadhouse).

What made the experience even better were the owners. They took the time to come over and talk with us, and they were seriously some of the coolest, most down-to-earth people. You can tell they genuinely care about their food, their customers, and what they’ve created. The whole atmosphere was warm, friendly, and welcoming, and the service was top notch.

This is exactly the kind of place you hope to stumble upon. Locally owned, unpretentious, incredible food, great people, and amazing quality tucked away in a small town. Front Street Cafe is truly a hidden gem. We will absolutely be back and I highly recommend it!

reviews.body: Avoid this place. The service here is a total mess. We weren't greeted or seated when we walked in, forcing us to sit at folding tables covered in cheap plastic tablecloths. The service was painfully slow; our drinks took forever, and the waitress ended up spilling water all over my friend. When we finally ordered, the kitchen was out of the specialty sauce for my $13 BLT, leaving me with a bland, overpriced sandwich. My friend's grilled cheese came out completely unmelted. For dessert, they served a terrible, cheap-tasting coconut pie that looked straight out of a dollar store. Do yourself a favor and eat somewhere else until management fixes this disaster.

reviews.name: Barry Sell

reviews.body:
Poor value for the price.I was disappointed with my choice today. The Parmesan Chicken Salad was mediocre and lacked flavor. It was missing the croutons, and the chicken portion was far too small, leaving me hungry afterward. At $16.99, the value just isn't there for the quality provided.

To clarify for anyone reading along:

I never said the food tasted "really good". I explicitly told whoever walked by—which I now realize was the owner, though it could have been anyone considering the lack of introduction—that it was just "alright" after some hesitation, and again to the server immediately after. I chose not to complain at the table because it simply wasn't worth my precious time to send it back and wait even longer. You had one job to deliver the meal properly, and it fell short.

Regarding the size:
if I was given a half portion, that is entirely on your kitchen—I ordered and paid for a full size. It is truly remarkable how a kitchen manages to forget key toppings on a $17 salad.

I write these reviews so I can remember my exact experiences if I ever think about lowering my standards enough to return. I completely stand by my original review.
Enjoy your day.

reviews.name: Greg Binkley

reviews.body:
This little gem in downtown Pemberville is everything you hope a true from-scratch kitchen will be. You can taste the difference in every bite; from the freshly baked breads to the farm-fresh eggs and locally sourced meats. They even fry in beef tallow, which says so much about their commitment to quality and using real, natural ingredients. The veggies and microgreens were incredibly fresh and flavorful.

The staff was warm, attentive, and genuinely caring, which made the whole experience even better. The dining room is small and cozy, tucked inside a charming old brick building that adds so much character. It feels welcoming and intentional, the kind of place you want to come back to again and again.

Joe nailed the cook on everything. Burger was a perfect medium all the way through. Soup, salads, fresh bread, just wonderful. And Jason gave us incredible service. We’ll be back, a lot.

Highly recommended if you appreciate thoughtfully prepared food made with integrity. Do not miss this one. Let’s encourage real food again, not the same old Sysco slop most places are slinging.

The service was warm, efficient, and friendly, and we even had the pleasure of meeting the owners, who were genuinely grateful for our visit. If you're looking for a gem in Pemberville, this small cafe delivers big on quality and hospitality.

reviews.body:
Stopped in with a longtime friend while my car was in the shop, and I’m so glad we finally made it in. I’ve known Brent for years but this was my first time visiting, and now I see why everyone raves about this place! The food was incredible—my eggs, bacon, and hash browns were cooked perfectly. I couldn’t resist grabbing a pecan cinnamon roll to go since I was too full to eat it there. Even a few hours later, it was still amazing—you can tell it’s made fresh in-house.

My friend had the biscuits and gravy and said they were the best ever. Joe was so friendly and knowledgeable, and he shared that the biscuits and gravy are homemade right there. It really shows.

Great food, great people, and such a welcoming spot. Brent and the whole team has built something special here. Can’t wait to come back to see as the place grows and evolves!

reviews.body: I usually try to find something positive to say on my reviews but this is tough.  The place was nice as far as the redecor they noted had been done recently.  The light blue with white accents was fresh and appealing, but the tables were not very clean.  They had one person seating, cleaning, taking orders, and checking customers out.  She was pleasant enough, but generally in no hurry to accommodate anyone and never checked on us aside from taking our order.  Had to actually walk up to the counter to ask for ketchup.  Coffee was nasty and I assure you we are not picky about our coffee.  Pop tasted funny - couldn't place why.  Food was mediocre at best, and the menu didn't have a number of the things that are pictured so beautifully on the website - including omelets.  At one point the server even started turning people away when they came in.  Very disappointing overall.

reviews.body: Just tried Front Street Cafe in Pemberville.   Great local eatery. They support local companies for as muas they can. All meat is from Frobose Meat Locker the coffee is Iron Bean which is veteran owned in Perrysburg.  All bread an baked goods are made in house. Definitely worth a try and worth it to support local

Very good food and with the right people it can explode with greatness.
